mechanism: Pair complete second/fourth rectangle bases with the half widths actually traversed by the two centre lines. Targets transferring a whole-width role into each receiver half and wrongly making the sum depend on the partition, E.
primary_math_proof: Let positive rectangle widths be a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=36. Original line one runs from centre(a) to centre(b): length a/2+b/2. Line two is c/2+d/2. Sum is18 regardless of four lengths, uniquely A. No coordinates of this particular illustrative partition are treated as givens. False full-to-half transfer gives a/2+b+c/2+d=18+(b+d)/2, which varies with widths and would support E. E is an anticipated mistaken dependence claim, not the actual geometry.

marker_roles.role: Blue source: full top edge of the second rectangle, b.
Blue receiver: portion of first centre line inside second rectangle, b/2, between existing dividing edge and original black centre.
Green source: full top edge of fourth rectangle, d.
Green receiver: portion of second centre line inside fourth rectangle, d/2.

human_semantics: Numerical ribbon length problem. Existing black centre dots, dividing lines and outer contour remain readable; no new line divides the ribbon. Colored portions are part of the original requested centre lines, so they remain included in the sum. Color preservation is not an output-picture selection constraint.
